examples.en: Today we study unit 5.
The grammar in this unit is difficult.

examples.ko: 시험 범위에 이 단원도 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This unit is also included in the exam range.
We take a quiz at the end of every unit.
The first unit of the book covers greetings.
The teacher gave homework for each unit.

explain: 단원은 교과서나 수업에서 내용을 주제별로 나눈 한 부분이에요. 소설 같은 책의 한 부분은 보통 '장'이라고 하고, 학교 교과서에서는 '단원'이라고 해요. '1단원', '단원 평가'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: We have the unit test for Unit 3 tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 단원을 공부한 뒤에 보는 시험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the test taken after finishing one unit.

phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자를 앞에 붙여 몇 번째 단원인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A number goes in front to say which unit it is.

phrases.en: The next unit will be easier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 단원 뒤에 나오는 단원을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the unit that comes after the current one.

explain_en: 단원 is one section of a textbook or course, divided by topic. A section in a novel-type book is usually called '장', while textbooks use 단원. Examples are '1단원' and '단원 평가'.

examples.en: The drama crew greeted the actors.

examples.ko: 제작진은 촬영 장소를 새로 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The crew is looking for a new filming location.

examples.ko: 이 영화 제작진에게 편지를 쓰고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to write a letter to the crew of this film.
Many viewers are cheering on the production team.
The whole crew edited the video all night.
The names of the crew appeared at the end of the broadcast.

explain: 제작진은 만드는 쪽(감독, 작가, 스태프)이고, 출연진은 화면에 나오는 쪽이에요. '제작진 여러분'처럼 한꺼번에 부를 때도 써요.

phrases.en: Everyone on the crew, thank you for your hard work today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제작진 모두를 한꺼번에 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to address the whole crew at once.

phrases.en: The film crew holds a press conference today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화를 만드는 사람들을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the people who make a film.

phrases.en: The crew and the cast took a photo together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만드는 쪽과 화면에 나오는 쪽을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the makers and the on-screen performers together.

explain_en: The 'jejakjin' is the making side (director, writer, staff), while 출연진 is the cast who appear on screen. You can also address everyone together as '제작진 여러분'.

examples.ko: 집배원이 등기를 가져왔는데 집에 아무도 없어서 못 받았어요.
examples.en: The mail carrier brought a registered letter, but nobody was home so I could not receive it.
I handed the letter to the mail carrier.
Mail carriers deliver mail even when it rains.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 집배원은 늘 인사를 잘해요.
examples.en: The mail carrier in our neighborhood always greets us nicely.

examples.ko: 집배원이 초인종을 눌러서 문을 열어 줬어요.
examples.en: The mail carrier rang the doorbell, so I opened the door.

examples.ko: 어머니는 집배원으로 십 년 넘게 일하셨어요.
examples.en: My mother worked as a mail carrier for over ten years.

explain: 직접 부를 때는 '집배원 아저씨/아주머니'라고 해요. '우체부'라고도 하는데 '집배원'이 지금 더 공식적인 말이에요. 일하는 곳은 '우체국'이에요.

phrases.en: The mail carrier brought a package for us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부르거나 친근하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when addressing or talking about the person in a friendly way.

phrases.en: In the old days, the mailman delivered letters by bicycle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '집배원'이 지금 더 공식적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 집배원 is the more formal word now.

phrases.en: The mail carrier delivered a letter to our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집배원이 하는 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used to describe what a mail carrier does.

explain_en: When addressing one directly, say '집배원 아저씨/아주머니'. '우체부' is also used, but '집배원' is the more official term now. They work at a '우체국' (post office).

examples.en: You must not cheat during the exam.

examples.ko: 옆 친구 답을 커닝하다가 선생님께 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I got caught by the teacher copying my neighbor's answers.

examples.ko: 저는 한 번도 커닝해 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never cheated even once.
Don't cheat; try to solve it on your own.
Nobody knows who cheated.

examples.ko: 시험 감독 선생님이 커닝하는 학생을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The proctor is looking for students who are cheating.

explain: '컨닝'이라고 잘못 쓰는 경우가 많은데 표준 표기는 '커닝'이에요. 시험에서 몰래 답을 보는 것에만 쓰고, 공식 문서에서는 '부정행위를 하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I have never cheated even once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정하는 말과 함께 써서 정직함을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used to say you were honest.

phrases.en: Please don't cheat during the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 규칙을 알려 줄 때 쓰는 정중한 금지 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite prohibition used when explaining exam rules.

phrases.example: 시험에서 부정행위를 하면 점수를 못 받아요.
phrases.en: If you cheat on a test, you can't get a score.

explain_en: Many people misspell it as '컨닝', but the standard spelling is '커닝'. It is used only for secretly looking at answers in a test, and formal documents say '부정행위를 하다' instead.
